output.brief: The latency jump is not caused by gateway 5.8. It was caused by the storage compaction tuning change pushed on the evening of 2 Nov. Evidence: in 11 cells the push raised compaction threads from 2 to 6. Disk use went from 41% to 97% within minutes, and node-side GET time went from 61 ms to 262 ms. Each cell's latency jumped within about 5–10 minutes of its own push, regardless of when 5.8 arrived. Cell aps-3 received 5.8 but skipped the push, and its latency stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. The network is clean. A fleet-wide rollback would not fix latency and would reopen the security flaw, which has a 30 Nov audit deadline. Do not pause compaction. Instead, revert the tuning in one cell first and watch GET p99 and backlog, then extend to the other cells. Compaction is still needed, since backlog is 4.0% now and the 15% danger point is not expected before 13 Nov. Hold off on limiting Orrin until the 10 Nov attribution report. Confidence is high, and the one-cell revert is the cheap confirming test.
